source.text: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις, ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς· Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον;

records.literal_gloss: And are gathered together to him the Pharisees and some of the scribes having come from Jerusalem \v 2 and having seen some of the disciples of him that with defiled hands, that is, unwashed, they eat the loaves \v 3 (for the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless with [the] fist they wash the hands, not eat, holding the tradition of the elders, \v 4 and from [the] marketplace, unless they wash themselves, not eat, and other things many there are which they received to hold, washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and couches) \v 5 and question him the Pharisees and the scribes, Why not walk the disciples of you according to the tradition of the elders, but with defiled hands eat the bread?

en.L: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gather to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 2 and [they] had seen that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples eat [their] bread with defiled hands, that is, unwashed \v 3 (for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash [their] hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders, \v 4 and [coming] from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash themselves, and there are many other things which they have received to hold to, washings of cups and pitchers and bronze vessels and couches), \v 5 and the Pharisees and the scribes question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat [their] bread with defiled hands?"
en.B: The Pharisees gathered around Jesus, together with some scribes who had come from Jerusalem. \v 2 They had noticed that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were eating their food with unclean hands, that is, hands not washed. \v 3 (The Pharisees, and indeed all the Jews, will not eat unless they give their hands a ritual washing, and so they keep the tradition of the elders. \v 4 When they come in from the marketplace they do not eat without first washing. They hold to many other customs that have been passed on to them as well, such as the washing of cups, pitchers, bronze pots and dining couches.) \v 5 So the Pharisees and the scribes put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not live by the tradition of the elders? Why do they eat with unclean hands?"
en.R: Some Pharisees and some teachers of God's law came from Jerusalem. They gathered around Jesus. \v 2 They saw that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were eating food without first washing their hands in the special religious way. \v 3 The Pharisees, like all Jewish people, would not eat unless they had washed their hands in this special way. In this way they kept the rules handed down by their teachers from long ago. \v 4 When they came home from the market, they would not eat until they had washed. They also kept many other rules like these. They washed cups, pitchers, and metal pots in a special way, and even the couches they lay on to eat. \v 5 So the Pharisees and the teachers of God's law asked Jesus, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not obey the rules our teachers handed down? They eat their food with hands that have not been made clean!"

vi.L: Và những người Pha-ri-si cùng một số thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến tụ họp quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 2 và [họ] đã thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn bánh bằng tay ô uế, nghĩa là [tay] chưa rửa \v 3 (vì những người Pha-ri-si và tất cả người Do Thái không ăn nếu không rửa tay bằng nắm tay, giữ theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, \v 4 và [khi] từ chợ [về], họ không ăn nếu không tẩy rửa mình, và còn nhiều điều khác họ đã nhận để giữ, [như] việc rửa chén, bình, nồi đồng và giường), \v 5 và những người Pha-ri-si cùng các thầy thông giáo hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao các môn đồ của Thầy không bước đi theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, nhưng ăn bánh bằng tay ô uế?"
vi.B: Những người Pha-ri-si và một số thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến tụ họp quanh Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Họ đã để ý thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn bằng tay ô uế, tức là tay chưa rửa. \v 3 (Những người Pha-ri-si, và cả mọi người Do Thái, không ăn nếu chưa rửa tay theo nghi thức; như thế họ giữ truyền thống của các trưởng lão. \v 4 Khi đi chợ về, họ cũng không ăn nếu chưa tẩy rửa. Họ còn giữ nhiều tập tục khác đã được truyền lại cho họ, như việc rửa chén, bình, nồi đồng và cả ghế dài để nằm ăn.) \v 5 Vì vậy, những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy thông giáo hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy không sống theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, mà lại ăn bằng tay ô uế?"
vi.R: Có mấy người Pha-ri-si và mấy thầy dạy luật từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến. Họ tụ họp quanh Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Họ thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn mà không rửa tay trước theo cách thức tôn giáo đặc biệt. \v 3 Người Pha-ri-si, cũng như mọi người Do Thái, không ăn nếu chưa rửa tay theo cách đặc biệt ấy. Làm như vậy là họ giữ những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại. \v 4 Khi đi chợ về, họ không ăn cho đến khi đã tẩy rửa. Họ còn giữ nhiều luật lệ khác giống như thế. Họ rửa chén, bình và nồi bằng kim loại theo một cách đặc biệt, và rửa cả những chiếc ghế dài họ nằm khi ăn. \v 5 Vì vậy, những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy dạy luật hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy không vâng theo những luật lệ các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại? Họ ăn bằng tay chưa được làm cho tinh sạch!"

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들과, 예루살렘에서 온 율법학자들 가운데 몇 사람이 그분께로 모여든다. \v 2 그들은 그분의 제자들 가운데 몇 사람이 부정한 손, 곧 씻지 않은 손으로 빵을 먹는 것을 보았다. \v 3 (바리새파 사람들과 모든 유대인은 장로들의 전통을 지켜서, 주먹으로 손을 씻지 않으면 먹지 않는다. \v 4 또 시장에서 [돌아오면] 몸을 씻지 않고는 먹지 않는다. 그 밖에도 그들이 지키도록 전해 받은 것이 많이 있는데, 잔과 단지와 놋그릇과 침상을 씻는 일이다.) \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 그분께 묻는다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 장로들의 전통을 따라 행하지 않고, 부정한 손으로 빵을 먹습니까?"
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들과, 예루살렘에서 내려온 율법학자 몇 사람이 예수 주위에 모여들었다. \v 2 그들은 예수의 제자들 가운데 몇 사람이 부정한 손, 곧 씻지 않은 손으로 음식을 먹는 것을 보았다. \v 3 (바리새파 사람들뿐 아니라 모든 유대인은 장로들의 전통을 지켜서, 정해진 방식대로 손을 씻지 않으면 음식을 먹지 않는다. \v 4 시장에서 돌아오면 먼저 몸을 씻지 않고는 먹지 않는다. 그 밖에도 그들이 물려받아 지키는 관습이 많은데, 잔과 단지와 놋그릇과 식사 때 기대는 침상을 씻는 일 같은 것이다.) \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 예수께 물었다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 장로들의 전통대로 살지 않습니까? 왜 부정한 손으로 음식을 먹습니까?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들과 율법을 가르치는 선생 몇 사람이 예루살렘에서 왔다. 그들이 예수 주위에 모였다. \v 2 그들은 예수의 제자 몇 사람이 손을 씻지 않고 음식을 먹는 것을 보았다. 종교 규칙에 따라 특별한 방식으로 손을 씻어야 하는데, 그렇게 하지 않은 것이다. \v 3 바리새파 사람들은, 다른 모든 유대인처럼, 이 특별한 방식으로 손을 씻지 않으면 음식을 먹지 않았다. 그렇게 해서 오래전 선생들이 물려준 규칙을 지켰다. \v 4 시장에 갔다가 집에 돌아오면, 씻기 전에는 먹지 않았다. 이런 규칙이 그 밖에도 많았다. 그들은 잔과 주전자와 쇠붙이 그릇을 특별한 방식으로 씻었고, 음식을 먹을 때 기대어 눕는 자리까지 씻었다. \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들이 예수께 물었다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 옛 선생들이 물려준 규칙을 지키지 않습니까? 왜 깨끗하게 씻지 않은 손으로 음식을 먹습니까?"

es.L: Y se reúnen junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los fariseos y algunos de los escribas que habían venido de Jerusalén, \v 2 y habían visto que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comen el pan con manos impuras, es decir, sin lavar \v 3 (porque los fariseos y todos los judíos no comen si no se lavan las manos con el puño, aferrándose a la tradición de los ancianos, \v 4 y [al volver] de la plaza no comen si no se lavan, y hay muchas otras cosas que recibieron para guardar: lavamientos de copas, de jarras, de vasijas de bronce y de lechos), \v 5 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntan los fariseos y los escribas: «¿Por qué no andan {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos conforme a la tradición de los ancianos, sino que comen el pan con manos impuras?».
es.B: Los fariseos se reunieron en torno a Jesús, junto con algunos escribas que habían venido de Jerusalén. \v 2 Habían notado que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comían con manos impuras, es decir, sin lavárselas. \v 3 (Los fariseos, y en realidad todos los judíos, no comen sin antes lavarse las manos con un lavado ritual, y así guardan la tradición de los ancianos. \v 4 Cuando vuelven del mercado, no comen sin lavarse primero. Y guardan muchas otras costumbres que les fueron transmitidas, como lavar copas, jarras, ollas de bronce y los divanes donde se reclinan para comer). \v 5 Así que los fariseos y los escribas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no viven según la tradición de los ancianos? ¿Por qué comen con manos impuras?».
es.R: Algunos fariseos y algunos maestros de la ley de Dios vinieron de Jerusalén y se reunieron alrededor de Jesús. \v 2 Vieron que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comían sin haberse lavado antes las manos con el lavado religioso especial. \v 3 Los fariseos, como todos los judíos, no comían si no se habían lavado las manos de esa manera especial. Así cumplían las reglas que les habían dejado sus maestros de tiempos antiguos. \v 4 Cuando volvían del mercado, no comían hasta haberse lavado. Además cumplían muchas otras reglas parecidas. Lavaban de una manera especial las copas, las jarras y las ollas de metal, y hasta los divanes en los que se recostaban para comer. \v 5 Entonces los fariseos y los maestros de la ley de Dios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron a Jesús: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no obedecen las reglas que nos dejaron nuestros maestros? ¡Comen con las manos sin purificar!».

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens et quelques-uns des scribes venus de Jérusalem se rassemblent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \v 2 et ayant vu que quelques-uns de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples mangent les pains avec des mains souillées, c’est-à-dire non lavées \v 3 (car les Pharisiens et tous les Juifs ne mangent pas sans s’être lavé les mains avec le poing, attachés à la tradition des anciens, \v 4 et [au retour] du marché, ils ne mangent pas sans s’être lavés, et il y a beaucoup d’autres choses qu’ils ont reçues pour les observer : lavages de coupes, de cruches, de vases de bronze et de lits), \v 5 et les Pharisiens et les scribes {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogent : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne marchent-ils pas selon la tradition des anciens, mais mangent-ils le pain avec des mains souillées ? »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens se rassemblèrent autour de Jésus, avec quelques scribes venus de Jérusalem. \v 2 Ils avaient remarqué que certains de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples prenaient leur repas avec des mains impures, c’est-à-dire non lavées. \v 3 (Les Pharisiens, comme d’ailleurs tous les Juifs, ne mangent pas sans s’être d’abord lavé les mains selon le rite ; ils restent ainsi fidèles à la tradition des anciens. \v 4 Quand ils rentrent du marché, ils ne mangent pas avant de s’être lavés. Ils observent encore bien d’autres coutumes qui leur ont été transmises, comme le lavage des coupes, des cruches, des pots de bronze et des lits de table.) \v 5 Les Pharisiens et les scribes {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} posèrent donc cette question : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne vivent-ils pas selon la tradition des anciens ? Pourquoi mangent-ils avec des mains impures ? »
fr.R: Des Pharisiens et des spécialistes de la Loi sont venus de Jérusalem. Ils se sont rassemblés autour de Jésus. \v 2 Ils ont vu que certains de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples mangeaient sans s’être lavé les mains de la façon prévue par la religion. \v 3 Les Pharisiens, comme tous les Juifs, ne mangeaient pas avant de s’être lavé les mains de cette façon spéciale. Ainsi, ils obéissaient aux règles transmises par leurs maîtres d’autrefois. \v 4 Quand ils revenaient du marché, ils ne mangeaient pas avant de s’être lavés. Ils suivaient aussi beaucoup d’autres règles de ce genre. Ils lavaient d’une façon spéciale les coupes, les cruches et les pots en métal, et même les lits sur lesquels ils s’allongeaient pour manger. \v 5 Alors les Pharisiens et les spécialistes de la Loi ont demandé à Jésus : « Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples n’obéissent pas aux règles que nos maîtres d’autrefois nous ont transmises ? Ils mangent avec des mains qui n’ont pas été purifiées ! »

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo na baadhi ya waandishi waliokuja kutoka Yerusalemu wanakusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, \v 2 nao walikuwa wameona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wanakula mikate [yao] kwa mikono najisi, yaani, isiyooshwa \v 3 (kwa maana Mafarisayo na Wayahudi wote hawali wasiponawa mikono kwa ngumi, wakishika mapokeo ya wazee, \v 4 na [wakitoka] sokoni hawali wasipojiosha, na kuna mambo mengine mengi waliyopokea ili wayashike: kuosha vikombe na mitungi na vyombo vya shaba na vitanda), \v 5 na Mafarisayo na waandishi wanamwuliza, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawaenendi kufuatana na mapokeo ya wazee, bali wanakula mikate [yao] kwa mikono najisi?"
sw.B: Mafarisayo walikusanyika kumzunguka Yesu, pamoja na baadhi ya waandishi waliokuwa wamekuja kutoka Yerusalemu. \v 2 Walikuwa wameona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakila chakula kwa mikono najisi, yaani, mikono isiyooshwa. \v 3 (Mafarisayo, na kwa kweli Wayahudi wote, hawali chakula bila kunawa mikono kwa taratibu za kidini; kwa njia hiyo wanashika mapokeo ya wazee. \v 4 Wanapotoka sokoni hawali kabla ya kujiosha. Pia wanashikilia desturi nyingine nyingi walizopokezwa, kama vile kuosha vikombe, mitungi, vyungu vya shaba na vitanda vya kuegemea wakati wa kula.) \v 5 Basi Mafarisayo na waandishi wakamwuliza Yesu, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawaishi kufuatana na mapokeo ya wazee? Kwa nini wanakula kwa mikono najisi?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo na baadhi ya walimu wa Sheria walikuja kutoka Yerusalemu. Wakakusanyika kumzunguka Yesu. \v 2 Waliona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakila chakula bila kwanza kunawa mikono kwa namna maalumu ya kidini. \v 3 Mafarisayo, kama Wayahudi wote, hawakula chakula kabla ya kunawa mikono kwa namna hiyo maalumu. Kwa njia hiyo walishika kanuni walizorithi kutoka kwa walimu wao wa zamani. \v 4 Waliporudi kutoka sokoni, hawakula mpaka wamejiosha kwanza. Walishika pia kanuni nyingine nyingi kama hizo. Waliosha vikombe, mitungi na vyungu vya shaba kwa namna maalumu, na hata vitanda walivyoegemea wakati wa kula. \v 5 Basi Mafarisayo na walimu wa Sheria wakamwuliza Yesu, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawashiki kanuni ambazo walimu wetu wa zamani walitupa? Wanakula chakula kwa mikono ambayo haijatakaswa!"

decisions.choice: are gathered, question: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they gathered, and they asked.

decisions.choice: defiled hands: hands that had not been washed by the ritual, so counted unclean, not dirty
decisions.reason: The word means common, ordinary, and so not set apart as clean. The washing was a religious rite, not a matter of hygiene. Mark explains this to readers who did not know Jewish custom.

decisions.choice: Mark stops the story to explain Jewish washing customs
decisions.reason: Verses 3-4 are Mark's note to his readers, many of whom were not Jews. The sentence that began in verse 1 is broken off and picked up again in verse 5.

decisions.choice: with the fist: a particular ritual way of washing, whose exact form is uncertain
alternatives: with a cupped handful of water
decisions.reason: The word means a fist. It may describe pouring water over the hands held in a fist, rubbing one fist in the other palm, or washing up to the wrist. All agree it names a set way of washing.

decisions.choice: with the fist, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "often" and a few leave the word out, perhaps because scribes found "with the fist" hard to understand. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the tradition of the elders: rules taught by earlier teachers and passed on by word of mouth
decisions.reason: The elders here are teachers of past generations. Their rulings, added to the law of Moses, were held by the Pharisees to be binding. The washing of hands before ordinary meals is not commanded in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: from the marketplace: when they come back from the market, they wash before eating
alternatives: they do not eat food from the market unless they wash it
decisions.reason: The words can be read either way. Most likely contact with many people at the market was thought to make a person unclean.

decisions.choice: wash themselves, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "sprinkle themselves". The SBLGNT reads the verb that means to wash or dip, the word from which baptize comes. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and couches: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts do not have "and couches", perhaps because scribes thought it strange to wash couches. The couches were those people reclined on to eat. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: give their hands a ritual washing
alternatives: wash their hands with the fist
decisions.reason: The exact sense of "with the fist" is unknown. Balanced gives what is certain: a set religious washing.

decisions.choice: the rules handed down by their teachers from long ago; the couches they lay on to eat
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the elders were and what couches were washed.

decisions.choice: "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "các thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes
alternatives: "các thầy dạy luật" at every level
decisions.reason: The forms the Vietnamese John already uses (8:3): the traditional title at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable a plain description of what these men did, teaching the law of Moses. "Kinh sư" is the Catholic word.

decisions.choice: "truyền thống của các trưởng lão" (L, B); "những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại" (R)
alternatives: "lời truyền khẩu của các bậc trưởng thượng"
decisions.reason: "Truyền thống" is the ordinary word for teaching handed down; "trưởng lão" keeps the Greek "elders". Readable says who the elders were, teachers of earlier times, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "tụ họp", "hỏi" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Mark tells these events in the present tense. Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps the vivid present by leaving out "đã", as the Vietnamese John does; the same holds for the other present-tense verbs of this chapter (7:18, 7:28, 7:32, 7:34).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("모여든다", "묻는다", "말씀하신다"), through chapter 7
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (7:1, 7:5, 7:18, 7:28, 7:32, 7:34); Balanced and Readable use the past, as in the Korean of chapter 3. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: "부정한 손" for the defiled (common) hands (L, B), explained in Readable; "장로들의 전통" (L, B), "오래전 선생들이 물려준 규칙" (R)
decisions.reason: The hands are ritually unclean, not dirty, so "부정한" (unclean in the religious sense) is used rather than "더러운"; the same root carries through "부정하게 하다" in 7:15-23. "장로들" keeps the word used for the elders of 8:31; Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees and scribes question Jesus in 합쇼체 but call him "당신", not "선생님"
alternatives: "선생님" as in the crowd's speech in 3:32
decisions.reason: The scene is hostile: they speak formally (합쇼체), as officials would, but keep their distance with "당신", as the unclean spirits do in 3:11. The style guide (section 4) allows this with a decision.

decisions.choice: present tense (L); past tense (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1 and John: Mark often tells his story in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it ("se reúnen", "preguntan"); Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories do. This applies throughout the chapter. Plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting, and every pronoun for Jesus that Spanish writes as a separate word takes the deity_pronoun setting, by the rule set for Mark at 1:2.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22: "escribas" is the word Spanish Bibles use; Readable says what these men were.

decisions.choice: manos impuras (L, B); sin purificar (R)
decisions.reason: The hands were not dirty but ritually unclean (meaning decision m2); Spanish "impuras" says that, where "sucias" would not.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B), with Literal keeping Mark’s present tense ("se rassemblent", "interrogent") and using the passé simple elsewhere; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole of Mark 7. The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken and school French. Literal keeps the present wherever Mark tells a past event in the present (7:1, 5, 18, 28, 32, 34), as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "des mains souillées" (L); "des mains impures" (B); "des mains qui n’ont pas été purifiées" (R)
decisions.reason: The hands were ritually unclean, not dirty (meaning decision on "defiled hands"). "Sales" would say dirt; Literal says "souillées", the word it keeps for the verb "defile" in 7:15-23, and Balanced "impures", the word it uses there for "make unclean".

decisions.choice: "les scribes" (L, B); "les spécialistes de la Loi" (R)
decisions.reason: As in French John (8:3): "scribe" today suggests a copyist, so Readable says what they were; "maîtres de la Loi" would clash with "Maître" as an address to Jesus, and "docteurs" now means physicians. Used for Mark as a whole.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanakusanyika, wanamwuliza); past at Balanced and Readable (walikusanyika, wakamwuliza)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present (meaning decision). Literal keeps it, as in the earlier chapters; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past with -li- and -ka-, as written Swahili narrative does. This holds for the whole of chapter 7.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (kwake, wake, wako)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("wanamwuliza", "walikusanyika kumzunguka"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer setting spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa Sheria (R)
alternatives: walimu wa Sheria at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22 and John 8:3: "waandishi" is the established Swahili name for the scribes; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of God's law".

decisions.choice: mikono najisi (unclean hands)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the hands were ritually unclean, not dirty. "Najisi" is the Swahili word for what is ritually unclean, while "michafu" would mean only that they needed soap. The same word, and the verb "kutia unajisi" / "kufanya najisi", carries 7:15-23.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi (disciples) at every level
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark, "wanafunzi" is plain enough for Readable, where the English Readable says "followers".

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν, ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Well prophesied Isaiah about you the hypocrites, as it has been written, This people with the lips me honors, but the heart of them far is away from me;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Well did Isaiah prophesy about you hypocrites, as it is written, 'This people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with [their] lips, but their heart is far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: He answered them, "How well Isaiah prophesied about you hypocrites! As it stands written: 'This people gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honor with their lips, while their heart stays far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus answered them, "You are hypocrites. You pretend to be good, but you are not. Isaiah was right about you when he spoke God's message long ago. He wrote down what God said: 'These people say that they honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but it is only words from their lips. Their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri đúng về các người, những kẻ giả hình, như có chép rằng: 'Dân này lấy môi tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri thật đúng về các người, những kẻ đạo đức giả! Như lời đã chép: 'Dân này tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng môi miệng, còn lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người là những kẻ đạo đức giả. Các người làm ra vẻ tốt lành, nhưng thật ra không phải vậy. Từ xưa, Ê-sai đã nói đúng về các người khi ông truyền lại sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời. Ông đã chép lại lời Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Dân này nói rằng họ tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng đó chỉ là lời nói ngoài môi miệng. Lòng họ thì ở xa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이사야가 너희 위선자들에 대하여 잘 예언하였다. 이렇게 기록되어 있다. '이 백성은 입술로 나를 공경하지만, 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "이사야가 너희 위선자들을 두고 참 잘 예언하였다! 기록된 대로이다. '이 백성은 입술로는 나를 높이지만, 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떠나 있다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 위선자들이다. 착한 척하지만 실제로는 그렇지 않다. 오래전에 이사야가 하나님의 말씀을 전했는데, 그 말이 너희에게 꼭 들어맞았다. 이사야는 하나님께서 하신 말씀을 이렇게 기록했다. '이 사람들은 나를 공경한다고 말하지만, 그것은 입술에서 나오는 말뿐이다. 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Bien profetizó Isaías acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hipócritas, como está escrito: “Este pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra con los labios, pero su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: Él les respondió: «¡Qué bien profetizó Isaías acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hipócritas! Así está escrito: “Este pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra con los labios, pero su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} unos hipócritas. {{plural_you:Aparentan|Aparentáis}} ser buenos, pero no lo {{plural_you:son|sois}}. Isaías tenía razón cuando, hace mucho tiempo, habló de parte de Dios acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él escribió lo que Dios dijo: “Esta gente dice que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, pero son solo palabras de sus labios. Su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Isaïe a bien prophétisé à votre sujet, hypocrites, comme il est écrit : “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore avec les lèvres, mais leur cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Comme Isaïe a bien prophétisé à votre sujet, hypocrites ! Il est écrit en effet : “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore de ses lèvres, mais son cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Vous êtes des hypocrites. Vous faites semblant d’être bons, mais vous ne l’êtes pas. Le prophète Isaïe avait raison à votre sujet quand il a transmis le message de Dieu, il y a longtemps. Il a écrit ce que Dieu disait : “Ces gens disent qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorent, mais ce ne sont que des mots sur leurs lèvres. Leur cœur est loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Isaya alitabiri vema kuhusu ninyi wanafiki, kama ilivyoandikwa, 'Watu hawa wananipa heshima kwa midomo, lakini moyo wao umekaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}};
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Isaya alitabiri sawasawa kabisa kuhusu ninyi wanafiki! Kama ilivyoandikwa: 'Watu hawa hunipa heshima kwa midomo yao, ilhali mioyo yao imekaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.
sw.R: Yesu akawajibu, "Ninyi ni wanafiki. Mnajifanya kuwa watu wema, lakini sivyo mlivyo. Zamani nabii Isaya alipotoa ujumbe wa Mungu, alisema kweli kuhusu ninyi. Aliandika maneno haya ya Mungu: 'Watu hawa wanasema kwamba wananiheshimu, lakini ni maneno ya midomo yao tu. Mioyo yao iko mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:13, in the wording of the ancient Greek translation
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes God's complaint through Isaiah against a people whose worship was only outward. The wording follows the Greek translation of Isaiah closely.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who play a part, whose outward show does not match the heart
decisions.reason: The word was used for an actor on a stage. The quotation shows the meaning: honor with the lips while the heart is far away. This is the only time Mark uses it.

decisions.choice: prophesied well: spoke God's word truly and to the point
decisions.reason: To prophesy is to speak for God. Isaiah's words fit the people of his own day, and Jesus says they fit these men too.

decisions.choice: lips and heart: God looks for worship that comes from within
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of thought and will. This prepares for 7:21, where evil comes from the heart.

decisions.choice: You pretend to be good, but you are not
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word hypocrite.

decisions.choice: say that they honor me, but it is only words from their lips
decisions.reason: Readable says what honoring with the lips means.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ giả hình" (L); "những kẻ đạo đức giả" (B, R)
alternatives: "những kẻ giả hình" at every level
decisions.reason: "Giả hình" is the familiar church word, kept at Literal; "đạo đức giả" is the everyday modern word for a person whose piety is a show, which is the sense the meaning decision gives.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the Pharisees and scribes "các người"; in the words of Isaiah God says "Ta"
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents and crowds, kept through the chapter (also 7:8-13 and to the crowd in 7:14). God speaking in Scripture says "Ta", with the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence.

decisions.choice: "위선자들" at every level; Readable adds what it means
decisions.reason: "위선자" is the current Korean word for one whose outward show does not match the heart; "외식하는 자" is the older church expression.

decisions.choice: « » for Jesus's words, “ ” for Isaiah
decisions.reason: The quotation of Isaiah inside Jesus's words takes the inner marks, as in Mark 1:2-3; Jesus's words run on to the end of 7:8. In Isaiah's words God speaks, so "me" and "mí" take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "leur cœur" (L); "son cœur" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek takes up the singular "people" with a plural "their"; Literal keeps the plural, which French allows for a people, and Balanced makes it agree with "ce peuple".

decisions.choice: wananipa heshima kwa midomo ... umekaa mbali nami
alternatives: the familiar wording of the Swahili Union Version
decisions.reason: Drafted from the Greek of Isaiah 29:13 as Mark quotes it, not from a Swahili Bible, whose familiar wording of this verse many readers know by heart. A reviewer should check that the wording reads naturally without echoing a copyrighted version.

decisions.choice: nami (with me), with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: In the quotation God is the speaker, so the joined pronoun "nami" takes the span, as the English "me" does.

source.text: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων·

records.literal_gloss: in vain and they worship me, teaching [as] teachings commands of men.

en.L: and in vain they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, teaching as doctrines the commands of {{gender:people|men}}.'
en.B: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is worthless, for they pass off human commands as doctrine.'
en.R: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is useless. They teach rules that people made up as if they were God's teaching.'

vi.L: và họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cách vô ích, dạy [như] giáo lý những điều răn của loài người.'
vi.B: Họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thật vô ích, vì họ lấy điều răn của loài người mà dạy như giáo lý.'
vi.R: Họ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng ích gì. Họ dạy những luật lệ do loài người đặt ra, như thể đó là lời dạy của Đức Chúa Trời.'

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 사람들의 계명들을 교훈으로 가르치며, 헛되이 나를 예배한다.'
ko.B: 그들이 나를 예배해도 아무 소용이 없다. 사람이 만든 계명을 하나님의 가르침처럼 가르치기 때문이다.'
ko.R: 그들이 나를 예배하는 것은 쓸모가 없다. 사람들이 지어낸 규칙을 하나님의 가르침인 것처럼 가르치기 때문이다.'

es.L: y en vano {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rinden culto, enseñando como doctrinas mandamientos de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}”.
es.B: En vano {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rinden culto, pues enseñan como doctrina lo que son mandatos humanos”.
es.R: De nada sirve que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adoren. Enseñan reglas inventadas por la gente como si fueran enseñanzas de Dios”.

fr.L: et c’est en vain qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent un culte, enseignant comme doctrines des commandements {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}.”
fr.B: Le culte qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent ne vaut rien, car ils font passer des commandements humains pour des doctrines.”
fr.R: C’est pour rien qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}adorent. Ils enseignent des règles inventées par des humains comme si c’était l’enseignement de Dieu.”

sw.L: na ni bure wanavyoniabudu, wakifundisha amri za wanadamu kama mafundisho.'
sw.B: Ibada yao {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} haina maana, kwa kuwa amri zilizotungwa na wanadamu wanazifundisha kana kwamba ni mafundisho ya Mungu.'
sw.R: Ibada yao {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} haifai kitu. Wanafundisha kanuni zilizotungwa na wanadamu kana kwamba ni mafundisho ya Mungu.'

decisions.choice: the end of Isaiah 29:13 in the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Isaiah says that their fear of God is a command of men learned by rote. The Greek translation, which Mark follows, says that their worship is in vain because they teach human commands. The sense is close.

decisions.choice: in vain: to no purpose, empty
decisions.reason: Their worship achieves nothing with God.

decisions.choice: teaching human commands as doctrines: passing off their own rules as God's teaching
decisions.reason: The verb takes two objects: what they teach, human commands, and what they present them as, doctrines.

decisions.choice: people (men as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, as against God.

decisions.choice: "loài người", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Loài người" (humankind) already takes in men and women, so the English gender setting has nothing to choose between in Vietnamese. The same holds for "loài người", "người ta" and "con người" through this chapter (7:8, 7:15, 7:18-23).

decisions.choice: "사람들" with no gender span, here and through chapter 7
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already includes men and women, so the English people/men span has no Korean counterpart (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings (meaning decision m3); the reader setting gives the traditional "los hombres". Balanced and Readable say "humanos" and "la gente", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word is the one for human beings ("men" in the general sense), so the default is inclusive and the traditional "d’hommes" is the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "humains", already inclusive, with no setting.

decisions.choice: wanadamu, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: "Wanadamu" (human beings) already includes men and women; the only male word, "wanaume", would change the meaning, so the gender setting has nothing to change in this chapter (also 7:8, 7:21).

source.text: ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: Having left the commandment of the God you hold the tradition of the men.

en.L: Leaving the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.B: You abandon what God has commanded and hold fast to a tradition that is merely human."
en.R: You put God's command to one side, and you hold on to rules that came from people."

vi.L: Bỏ điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời, các người giữ truyền thống của loài người."
vi.B: Các người bỏ qua điều Đức Chúa Trời truyền dạy mà giữ chặt truyền thống chỉ do loài người đặt ra."
vi.R: Các người gạt điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời sang một bên, rồi bám lấy những luật lệ do loài người đặt ra."

ko.L: 너희는 하나님의 계명을 버리고 사람들의 전통을 붙잡고 있다."
ko.B: 너희는 하나님의 명령은 저버리고, 사람에게서 나온 전통만 굳게 지키고 있다."
ko.R: 너희는 하나님의 명령은 제쳐 두고, 사람들이 만든 규칙은 꼭 붙들고 있다."

es.L: Dejando el mandamiento de Dios, {{plural_you:se aferran|os aferráis}} a la tradición de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}».
es.B: {{plural_you:Abandonan|Abandonáis}} lo que Dios ha mandado y {{plural_you:se aferran|os aferráis}} a una tradición que es solo humana».
es.R: {{plural_you:Dejan|Dejáis}} de lado el mandamiento de Dios y {{plural_you:se aferran|os aferráis}} a reglas que vienen de la gente».

fr.L: Ayant laissé le commandement de Dieu, vous tenez ferme la tradition {{gender:des humains|des hommes}}. »
fr.B: Vous abandonnez le commandement de Dieu et vous vous attachez à une tradition purement humaine. »
fr.R: Vous mettez de côté le commandement de Dieu, et vous vous accrochez à des règles qui viennent des humains. »

sw.L: Mkiiacha amri ya Mungu, mnashikilia mapokeo ya wanadamu."
sw.B: Mnaweka kando kile ambacho Mungu ameamuru, na kushikilia mapokeo ambayo ni ya kibinadamu tu."
sw.R: Mnaiweka amri ya Mungu pembeni, na kushikilia kanuni zilizotoka kwa wanadamu."

decisions.choice: leaving: abandoning, letting go
decisions.reason: The verb can mean forgive, but here it means to leave behind or neglect.

decisions.choice: the commandment of God: God's law as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular sums up what God has commanded. Verse 10 gives an example.

decisions.choice: God's command against human tradition: the contrast that runs through 7:8-13
decisions.reason: Jesus does not reject every custom. He rejects tradition that is held in place of God's command.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the verse at "the tradition of men"
alternatives: add: the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other such things you do
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add these words, which repeat 7:4 and 7:13. They are not in the earliest manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a tradition that is merely human
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the contrast with God's command.

decisions.choice: mapokeo (L, B); kanuni (R)
decisions.reason: "Mapokeo" (what is handed down) is the Swahili word for tradition, used in Galatians 1:14 and Colossians 2:8. Readable says "kanuni" (rules), as the English Readable says "rules".

source.text: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν τηρήσητε·

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Well you set aside the commandment of the God so that the tradition of you you might keep.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Well do you set aside the commandment of God, so that you may keep your tradition.
en.B: He went on, "You are very skillful at setting God's command aside so that you can keep your own tradition!
en.R: Jesus went on, "You are very clever! You find ways to ignore what God commands so that you can keep your own rules.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Các người khéo gạt bỏ điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời, để giữ truyền thống của các người.
vi.B: Ngài nói tiếp: "Các người thật khéo léo gạt bỏ điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời để giữ lấy truyền thống của mình!
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói tiếp: "Các người thật là khôn khéo! Các người tìm cách lờ đi điều Đức Chúa Trời truyền dạy để giữ những luật lệ riêng của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 너희의 전통을 지키려고 하나님의 계명을 잘도 저버린다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀을 이어 가셨다. "너희는 너희 전통을 지키려고 하나님의 명령을 참 교묘하게도 저버린다!
ko.R: 예수께서 계속 말씀하셨다. "너희는 참 영리하구나! 너희 규칙을 지키려고, 하나님께서 명령하신 것을 무시할 방법을 찾아내는구나.

es.L: Y les decía: «Bien {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} sin efecto el mandamiento de Dios para guardar {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición.
es.B: Y añadió: «¡Qué hábiles {{plural_you:son|sois}} para dejar a un lado el mandamiento de Dios y así guardar {{plural_you:su propia|vuestra propia}} tradición!
es.R: Jesús siguió diciendo: «¡Qué astutos {{plural_you:son|sois}}! {{plural_you:Encuentran|Encontráis}} maneras de no hacer caso a lo que Dios manda para poder cumplir {{plural_you:sus propias|vuestras propias}} reglas.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « Vous mettez bien de côté le commandement de Dieu, afin de garder votre tradition.
fr.B: Il ajouta : « Vous savez fort bien écarter le commandement de Dieu pour garder votre propre tradition !
fr.R: Jésus a continué : « Vous êtes très habiles ! Vous trouvez toujours un moyen de ne pas tenir compte de ce que Dieu commande, pour pouvoir garder vos propres règles.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia, "Vema mnaikataa amri ya Mungu, ili mshike mapokeo yenu.
sw.B: Akaendelea kusema, "Ninyi ni hodari kweli wa kuiweka kando amri ya Mungu ili mshike mapokeo yenu wenyewe!
sw.R: Yesu akaendelea kusema, "Ninyi ni wajanja sana! Mnatafuta njia za kupuuza amri ya Mungu ili mshike kanuni zenu wenyewe.

decisions.choice: well: said with irony, how cleverly
decisions.reason: The same word as in 7:6, now turned against them: they are skilled at the wrong thing.

decisions.choice: set aside: reject, treat as void
decisions.reason: The verb is used for refusing or cancelling something that has force.

decisions.choice: keep, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "establish" your tradition. The two words differ by little in Greek. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: very skillful (B); very clever (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the irony of "well" plain.

decisions.choice: "khéo" (L); "thật khéo léo" (B); "thật là khôn khéo" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "khéo" can praise or mock, so it carries the irony of the Greek "well" (meaning decision) without a word that sounds like plain praise.

decisions.choice: "잘도" for the ironic "well"
decisions.reason: Korean "잘도" carries the irony of the Greek "well" (how cleverly) while keeping the word; plain "잘" would sound like praise.

decisions.choice: Bien (L); ¡Qué hábiles ...! (B); ¡Qué astutos! (R)
decisions.reason: The word is ironic (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the plain "bien"; Balanced and Readable make the irony plain with an exclamation.

source.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·

records.literal_gloss: Moses for said, Honor the father of you and the mother of you, and, The [one] speaking evil of father or mother by death let him end.

en.L: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'
en.B: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and also, 'Whoever reviles father or mother is to die for it.'
en.R: Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who says evil things against their father or mother is to be put to death.'

vi.L: Vì Môi-se đã nói: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mình và mẹ mình,' và: 'Kẻ nào nói xấu cha hoặc mẹ thì phải chết.'
vi.B: Vì Môi-se đã nói: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mẹ mình,' và: 'Ai chửi rủa cha hoặc mẹ phải bị xử tử.'
vi.R: Môi-se đã nói: 'Hãy tôn kính cha mẹ mình.' Ông cũng nói: 'Ai nói những lời độc ác xúc phạm cha hoặc mẹ mình thì phải bị xử tử.'

ko.L: 모세가 '네 아버지와 네 어머니를 공경하여라' 하고 말하였고, 또 '아버지나 어머니를 악하게 말하는 사람은 반드시 죽어야 한다' 하고 말하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 모세는 '네 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라' 하였고, 또 '아버지나 어머니를 모욕하는 사람은 반드시 사형에 처해야 한다' 하였다.
ko.R: 모세는 '너희 아버지와 어머니를 공경하여라' 하고 말했다. 또 '자기 아버지나 어머니를 나쁘게 말하는 사람은 사형에 처해야 한다' 하고 말했다.

es.L: Porque Moisés dijo: “Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”, y: “El que hable mal de padre o de madre, que muera sin remedio”.
es.B: Porque Moisés dijo: “Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”, y también: “El que insulte a su padre o a su madre será condenado a muerte”.
es.R: Moisés dijo: “Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”. También dijo: “Al que hable mal de su padre o de su madre, hay que darle muerte”.

fr.L: Car Moïse a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et : “Celui qui dit du mal de [son] père ou de [sa] mère doit être puni de mort.”
fr.B: Moïse a dit en effet : “Honore ton père et ta mère”, et aussi : “Celui qui insulte son père ou sa mère doit être mis à mort.”
fr.R: Moïse a dit : “Honore ton père et ta mère.” Il a dit aussi : “Celui qui dit du mal de son père ou de sa mère doit être puni de mort.”

sw.L: Kwa maana Musa alisema, 'Mheshimu baba yako na mama yako,' na, 'Anayesema maovu juu ya baba au mama, lazima afe.'
sw.B: Kwa maana Musa alisema, 'Mheshimu baba yako na mama yako,' na tena, 'Mtu anayemtukana baba au mama yake na auawe.'
sw.R: Musa alisema, 'Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako.' Pia alisema, 'Mtu yeyote anayesema maneno mabaya dhidi ya baba yake au mama yake ni lazima auawe.'

decisions.choice: honor your father and your mother: the fifth commandment, Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the commandment the word of Moses here and the word of God in 7:13.

decisions.choice: whoever speaks evil of father or mother: Exodus 21:17; Leviticus 20:9
decisions.reason: The law treated cursing a parent as a crime deserving death.

decisions.choice: honor: respect, and also support and care for parents in old age
decisions.reason: Honoring parents included providing for them. This is the point of the example in 7:11-12.

decisions.choice: end by death: surely die, be put to death
decisions.reason: The words copy a Hebrew way of speaking that stresses certainty. The law means the death penalty.

decisions.choice: reviles
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak evil of someone, to abuse with words.

decisions.choice: "cha mình và mẹ mình" (L); "cha mẹ mình" (B, R) for "your father and your mother"
decisions.reason: "Ngươi" is archaic, and "con" or "anh" would fix a relation that the commandment, said to every reader, does not have; the reflexive "mình" speaks to whoever hears it. Balanced and Readable use the usual pair "cha mẹ".

decisions.choice: que muera sin remedio (L); será condenado a muerte (B); hay que darle muerte (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew way of saying "he shall surely die" (meaning decision m4); each level says it in plain Spanish, without the old "morirá de muerte".

decisions.choice: "doit être puni de mort" (L, R); "doit être mis à mort" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek "let him end by death" is an idiom for a sure death sentence (meaning decision); a word-for-word "mourir de mort" is not French, so every level states the penalty.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Κορβᾶν, ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς, οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί, ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε· καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: You but say, If says a man to the father or the mother, Corban, which is, Gift, whatever from me you might be benefited, \v 12 no longer you allow him anything to do for the father or the mother, \v 13 making void the word of the God by the tradition of you which you handed down; and similar such things many you do.

en.L: But you say, 'If a person says to father or mother, "Whatever you might have gained from me [is] Corban," which is, a gift [to God],' \v 12 you no longer let that person do anything for father or mother, \v 13 making void the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down; and you do many similar things such as these."
en.B: But you teach that if someone tells father or mother, 'Whatever support you could have had from me is Corban' (which means an offering to God), \v 12 then you no longer let that person do anything for their father or mother. \v 13 You make God's word empty for the sake of the tradition you hand down, and you do plenty of other things of the same kind."
en.R: But you teach something else. You say that a person can tell their father or mother, 'I cannot help you, because what I would have given you is Corban.' Corban means a gift set apart for God. \v 12 After that, you will not let them do anything to help their father or mother. \v 13 So by keeping the rules you pass down, you make God's word count for nothing. And you do many other things like that."

vi.L: Nhưng các người nói: 'Nếu một người nói với cha hoặc mẹ: "Bất cứ điều gì cha mẹ có thể được con giúp, là Cọt-ban," nghĩa là của lễ [dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời],' \v 12 thì các người không còn để người ấy làm gì cho cha hoặc mẹ nữa, \v 13 [như vậy] làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời ra vô hiệu bởi truyền thống mà các người đã truyền lại; và các người làm nhiều điều tương tự như thế."
vi.B: Nhưng các người lại dạy rằng nếu ai nói với cha hoặc mẹ: 'Những gì con có thể giúp cha mẹ đều là Cọt-ban' (nghĩa là của lễ dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời), \v 12 thì các người không cho người ấy làm gì cho cha mẹ mình nữa. \v 13 Như vậy, vì truyền thống các người truyền lại, các người làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời ra vô hiệu. Các người còn làm nhiều điều khác giống như thế."
vi.R: Nhưng các người lại dạy khác. Các người nói rằng một người có thể nói với cha mẹ mình: 'Con không giúp cha mẹ được, vì những gì con định biếu cha mẹ là Cọt-ban.' Cọt-ban nghĩa là của lễ đã dành riêng cho Đức Chúa Trời. \v 12 Sau đó, các người không cho người ấy làm gì để giúp cha mẹ mình nữa. \v 13 Như vậy, vì giữ những luật lệ các người truyền lại, các người làm cho lời Đức Chúa Trời trở thành vô giá trị. Các người còn làm nhiều việc khác giống như thế."

ko.L: 그런데 너희는 말한다. '누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 "제게서 받으실 수 있는 것은 무엇이든 고르반, 곧 [하나님께 드린] 예물입니다" 하고 말하면,' \v 12 너희는 그 사람이 아버지나 어머니를 위하여 더 이상 아무것도 하지 못하게 한다. \v 13 이렇게 너희는 너희가 전해 준 너희 전통으로 하나님의 말씀을 무효로 만든다. 그리고 너희는 이와 비슷한 일들을 많이 한다."
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 이렇게 가르친다. 누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 '제가 드릴 수 있었던 도움은 무엇이든 고르반입니다' 하고 말하면(고르반은 하나님께 바친 예물이라는 뜻이다), \v 12 너희는 그 사람이 더 이상 아버지나 어머니를 위해 아무것도 하지 못하게 한다. \v 13 너희는 이렇게 너희가 물려주는 전통을 내세워 하나님의 말씀을 헛되게 만든다. 그리고 이와 비슷한 일을 많이 한다."
ko.R: 그런데 너희는 다르게 가르친다. 누구든지 아버지나 어머니에게 '제가 도와 드리려던 것은 고르반이어서 도와 드릴 수 없습니다' 하고 말해도 된다고 한다. 고르반은 하나님께 바치려고 따로 떼어 놓은 선물이라는 뜻이다. \v 12 그렇게 말하고 나면, 너희는 그 사람이 아버지나 어머니를 돕지 못하게 한다. \v 13 이렇게 너희는 너희가 물려주는 규칙을 지키느라 하나님의 말씀을 쓸모없게 만든다. 그리고 이런 일을 그 밖에도 많이 한다."

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Si alguien dice al padre o a la madre: ‘Es corbán (es decir, ofrenda [a Dios]) cualquier ayuda que pudieras recibir de mí’”, \v 12 ya no le {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} hacer nada por el padre o la madre, \v 13 anulando la palabra de Dios con {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición que {{plural_you:han transmitido|habéis transmitido}}. Y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} muchas cosas parecidas a estas».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes enseñan|vosotros enseñáis}} que, si alguien le dice a su padre o a su madre: “Cualquier ayuda que pudieras recibir de mí es corbán” (es decir, una ofrenda para Dios), \v 12 entonces ya no le {{plural_you:permiten|permitís}} hacer nada por su padre o por su madre. \v 13 Así {{plural_you:anulan|anuláis}} la palabra de Dios por causa de la tradición que {{plural_you:transmiten|transmitís}}, y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} muchas otras cosas parecidas».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes enseñan|vosotros enseñáis}} otra cosa. {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}} que una persona puede decirle a su padre o a su madre: “No puedo ayudarte, porque lo que te habría dado es corbán”. Corbán quiere decir un regalo apartado para Dios. \v 12 Después de eso, ya no le {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} hacer nada para ayudar a su padre o a su madre. \v 13 Así, por cumplir las reglas que {{plural_you:se pasan|os pasáis}} de unos a otros, {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} que la palabra de Dios no valga nada. Y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} muchas otras cosas como esa».

fr.L: Mais vous, vous dites : “Si {{gender:une personne|un homme}} dit à [son] père ou à [sa] mère : ‘Ce dont tu aurais pu profiter de ma part [est] Corban’, c’est-à-dire offrande [à Dieu]”, \v 12 vous ne lui permettez plus de rien faire pour [son] père ou [sa] mère, \v 13 annulant la parole de Dieu par votre tradition, que vous avez transmise ; et vous faites beaucoup de choses semblables à celles-là. »
fr.B: Mais vous, vous enseignez que si quelqu’un dit à son père ou à sa mère : “L’aide que tu aurais pu recevoir de moi est Corban” (c’est-à-dire offrande à Dieu), \v 12 alors vous ne lui permettez plus de rien faire pour son père ou sa mère. \v 13 Ainsi vous videz la parole de Dieu de sa force au profit de la tradition que vous transmettez. Et vous faites bien d’autres choses du même genre. »
fr.R: Mais vous, vous enseignez autre chose. Vous dites que quelqu’un peut dire à son père ou à sa mère : “Je ne peux pas t’aider, parce que ce que je t’aurais donné est Corban.” Corban veut dire un don réservé à Dieu. \v 12 Après cela, vous ne laissez plus cette personne aider son père ou sa mère. \v 13 Ainsi, en suivant les règles que vous transmettez, vous enlevez toute valeur à la parole de Dieu. Et vous faites beaucoup d’autres choses de ce genre. »

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mnasema, 'Mtu akimwambia baba au mama, "Chochote ambacho ungefaidika nacho kutoka kwangu [ni] Korbani," yaani, zawadi [kwa Mungu],' \v 12 hammruhusu tena kufanya lolote kwa ajili ya baba au mama, \v 13 mkilitangua neno la Mungu kwa mapokeo yenu mliyoyapokeza; na mnafanya mambo mengi yanayofanana na hayo."
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mnafundisha kwamba mtu akimwambia baba au mama yake, 'Msaada wowote ambao ungepata kutoka kwangu ni Korbani' (maana yake, sadaka iliyotolewa kwa Mungu), \v 12 basi hammruhusu tena kufanya chochote kwa ajili ya baba au mama yake. \v 13 Mnalifanya neno la Mungu kuwa bure kwa ajili ya mapokeo mnayoyapokezana, na mnafanya mambo mengine mengi ya namna hiyo."
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mnafundisha jambo lingine. Mnasema kwamba mtu anaweza kumwambia baba yake au mama yake, 'Siwezi kukusaidia, kwa sababu kile ambacho ningekupa ni Korbani.' Korbani maana yake ni zawadi iliyotengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu. \v 12 Baada ya hapo hammruhusu tena mtu huyo kufanya lolote kuwasaidia baba yake au mama yake. \v 13 Hivyo kwa kushika kanuni mnazopokezana, mnalifanya neno la Mungu kuwa si kitu. Nanyi mnafanya mambo mengine mengi kama hayo."

decisions.choice: Corban: a word for an offering dedicated to God, kept and translated by Mark
decisions.reason: The word is used in the law of Moses for an offering brought to God (Leviticus 2:1). A man could declare his goods Corban, set apart for God, and so put them beyond his parents' reach, while he may still have kept the use of them.

decisions.choice: the sentence is left unfinished: Jesus states their rule, then says what follows from it
decisions.reason: The teachers' rule is "if anyone says Corban, the vow stands". Jesus breaks off and states the result: you no longer allow him to help his parents.

decisions.choice: making void: cancelling, taking away the force of
decisions.reason: The word was used for annulling a law or a contract.

decisions.choice: the word of God: the commandment Moses gave (7:10)
decisions.reason: What Moses said in 7:10 Jesus calls the word of God, set against the tradition handed down by people.

decisions.choice: Corban, kept as Mark keeps it
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Hebrew word and explains it, so every level does the same.

decisions.choice: I cannot help you, because
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vow meant for the parents.

decisions.choice: "Cọt-ban"
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Hebrew word and explains it; Vietnamese keeps it too, in the transliteration the Protestant tradition uses, followed by Mark's explanation.

decisions.choice: The son speaks to his parent as "cha mẹ" and of himself as "con"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a pronoun for the singular "you" and for "me"; a child speaking to a father or mother says "cha mẹ" and "con". "Cha mẹ" also covers "father or mother" without naming one.

decisions.choice: "고르반", the Protestant spelling of Corban, kept at every level
decisions.reason: Korean readers know the word in this form; Mark explains it himself, and Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: The son speaks to his parents in 합쇼체 ("제게서", "예물입니다")
decisions.reason: A grown child speaking a formal vow to father or mother would use the deferential style; this keeps the quoted vow polite while its content is harsh.

decisions.choice: corbán
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Hebrew word and explains it (meaning decision m1); Spanish does the same, writing it in lower case as an ordinary word.

decisions.choice: ‘ ’ inside “ ” inside « »
decisions.reason: The vow quoted inside the Pharisees' teaching, which is quoted inside Jesus's words, takes a third level of quotation marks, as in John 10:34.

decisions.choice: {{gender:une personne|un homme}} (L); "quelqu’un" with no setting (B, R)
alternatives: no setting at Literal, as in English
decisions.reason: The Greek has the noun for a human being; French Literal needs a noun for it, so the gender setting goes there, with the traditional "un homme" as the alternative. The pronoun "lui" that follows is the same for both. Balanced and Readable say "quelqu’un", already inclusive.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks ‘ ’ for the words spoken inside the quoted rule
decisions.reason: Literal keeps three levels of speech (Jesus, their rule, the son’s vow). French uses « » and then “ ”; the third level takes ‘ ’ so the reader can see where the vow ends. Balanced and Readable need only two levels.

decisions.choice: Korbani
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the word and explains it (meaning decision), so Swahili keeps it too, with the final -i that Swahili gives to borrowed names (as Beelzebuli in 3:22).

source.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ σύνετε.

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] again the crowd he was saying to them, Hear me all and understand.

en.L: And calling the crowd to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all [of you], and understand:
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called the crowd to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} once more and said, "Hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, every one of you, and understand this:
en.R: Then Jesus called the crowd to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again. He said, "Everyone, listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and try to understand.

vi.L: Và gọi đoàn dân đến [với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] một lần nữa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Hết thảy các người hãy nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và hiểu:
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại gọi đoàn dân đến và nói: "Tất cả các người hãy nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và hiểu điều này:
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu lại gọi đoàn dân đến gần. Ngài nói: "Mọi người hãy nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cố gắng hiểu.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 다시 무리를 [가까이] 불러 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 모두 내 말을 듣고 깨달아라.
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 무리를 가까이 부르시고 말씀하셨다. "너희는 모두 내 말을 듣고 깨달아라.
ko.R: 예수께서 사람들을 다시 가까이 부르셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "모두 내 말을 잘 듣고, 깨달으려고 애써 보아라.

es.L: Y llamando otra vez a la multitud, les decía: «{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} todos, y {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}}:
es.B: Luego llamó de nuevo a la multitud y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} todos, y {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}} esto:
es.R: Entonces Jesús volvió a llamar a la gente para que se acercara a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} todos y {{plural_you:traten|tratad}} de entender.

fr.L: Et ayant appelé de nouveau la foule, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} tous, et comprenez.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela de nouveau la foule et dit : « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous tous, et comprenez bien ceci :
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a de nouveau appelé la foule. Il a dit : « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous tous, et essayez de comprendre.

sw.L: Na akiuita umati tena [uje] {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, alikuwa akiwaambia, "Nisikilizeni, nyote, na mwelewe:
sw.B: Kisha akauita umati tena uje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akasema, "Nisikilizeni, kila mmoja wenu, mwelewe jambo hili:
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akauita umati wa watu uje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} tena. Akasema, "Nisikilizeni nyote, na jitahidini kuelewa.

decisions.choice: again: once more Jesus calls the crowd to hear
alternatives: the crowd had been there all along
decisions.reason: The crowd were last named in 6:55-56. Jesus now turns from the Pharisees to teach everyone.

decisions.choice: understand: grasp the meaning
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 4:12 and 6:52. The disciples will show in 7:18 that they have not understood.

decisions.choice: try to understand
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this is a call to think carefully.

decisions.choice: "Mọi người" (R) for "all of you"
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the crowd with the neutral "mọi người" (everyone), which a plain reader hears as an invitation; Literal and Balanced keep the book's "các người".

decisions.choice: llamando ... a la multitud
decisions.reason: Spanish "llamar" already means calling someone to oneself, so Literal needs no bracketed "to him".

source.text: οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν· ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: Nothing there is from outside the man entering into him which is able to defile him; but the things out of the man going out are the things defiling the man.

en.L: There is nothing from outside the person that enters into {{gender:them|him}} which can defile {{gender:them|him}}; but the things coming out of the person are the things that defile the person."
en.B: Nothing outside a person can make that person unclean by going in. What comes out of a person is what makes a person unclean."
en.R: Nothing that goes into people from the outside can make them unclean before God. It is the things that come out of people that make them unclean."

vi.L: Không có gì từ bên ngoài con người đi vào trong người ấy mà có thể làm người ấy ô uế; nhưng những gì từ trong con người đi ra, ấy là những điều làm con người ô uế."
vi.B: Không có gì ở bên ngoài đi vào trong một người mà có thể làm cho người ấy ô uế. Chính những gì từ trong một người đi ra mới làm cho người ấy ô uế."
vi.R: Không có gì từ bên ngoài đi vào trong người ta mà có thể làm cho họ ra ô uế trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời. Chính những gì từ bên trong con người đi ra mới làm cho họ ô uế."

ko.L: 사람 밖에서 그 사람 안으로 들어가는 것 가운데 그를 부정하게 할 수 있는 것은 아무것도 없다. 오히려 사람에게서 나오는 것들, 그것들이 사람을 부정하게 하는 것이다."
ko.B: 밖에서 사람 안으로 들어가는 것은 무엇이든 그 사람을 부정하게 할 수 없다. 사람에게서 나오는 것, 그것이 사람을 부정하게 한다."
ko.R: 밖에서 사람의 몸속으로 들어가는 것은 사람을 하나님 앞에서 더럽게 만들 수 없다. 사람에게서 나오는 것이 사람을 더럽게 만든다."

es.L: No hay nada fuera de la persona que, entrando en ella, pueda contaminarla; sino que lo que sale de la persona es lo que contamina a la persona».
es.B: Nada de lo que está fuera de una persona puede hacerla impura al entrar en ella. Lo que sale de la persona es lo que la hace impura».
es.R: Nada de lo que entra en la gente desde afuera puede hacerla impura ante Dios. Lo que sale de las personas es lo que las hace impuras».

fr.L: Il n’y a rien hors de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} qui, entrant en lui, puisse le souiller ; mais ce qui sort de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}, c’est cela qui souille {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}. »
fr.B: Rien de ce qui, venant du dehors, entre en quelqu’un ne peut le rendre impur. C’est ce qui sort de quelqu’un qui le rend impur. »
fr.R: Ce qui entre dans les gens, depuis l’extérieur, ne peut pas les rendre impurs aux yeux de Dieu. Ce qui les rend impurs, c’est ce qui sort d’eux. »

sw.L: Hakuna kitu kilicho nje ya mtu ambacho kikiingia ndani yake kinaweza kumtia unajisi; bali vitu vinavyotoka ndani ya mtu ndivyo vinavyomtia mtu unajisi."
sw.B: Hakuna kitu kilicho nje ya mtu kinachoweza kumfanya najisi kwa kuingia ndani yake. Kinachotoka ndani ya mtu ndicho kinachomfanya mtu kuwa najisi."
sw.R: Hakuna kitu kinachoingia ndani ya mtu kutoka nje kinachoweza kumfanya najisi mbele za Mungu. Ni yale yanayotoka ndani ya mtu ndiyo yanayomfanya najisi."

decisions.choice: defile: make common, that is, ritually unclean
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for the "defiled" hands of 7:2. Unclean means unfit to come before God in worship.

decisions.choice: the man: any human being
decisions.reason: The word means a person, man or woman.

decisions.choice: true uncleanness comes from within, not from food
alternatives: a teaching only about washing hands
decisions.reason: Jesus goes further than the question about hands. What enters the body cannot make a person unclean; what comes from the heart does (7:21-23). Mark draws out the meaning for food in 7:19.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 16
alternatives: add verse 16: If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add verse 16, "If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear." It is missing from the earliest manuscripts and was most likely copied from 4:9 and 4:23, where Jesus says the same after a parable. The SBLGNT leaves it out, so the verse number 16 is skipped. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: them (him as the alternative) in Literal; a person, people in Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The saying is about every person, so the wording is inclusive.

decisions.choice: unclean before God
decisions.reason: Readable says before whom a person is unclean.

decisions.choice: "ô uế" for "defile" / "unclean", at every level
decisions.reason: "Ô uế" is uncleanness in the religious sense, which is the point (meaning decision); "dơ bẩn" would suggest dirt. The same word is used in 7:2, 7:5 and 7:18-23 so the thread of the passage stays visible.

decisions.choice: "부정하게 하다" (L, B); "하나님 앞에서 더럽게 만들다" (R) for defile, through 7:23
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the link with the "부정한 손" of 7:2, since the Greek uses the same root; Readable uses the plainer "더럽게" and says it is about standing before God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la persona ... -la; no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "persona" is feminine whoever is meant, so the pronouns that refer to it are already inclusive and need no setting.

decisions.choice: contaminar (L); hacer impuro (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means to make ritually unclean (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps one verb throughout 7:15-23; Balanced and Readable say "hacer impuro", which ties it to the "manos impuras" of 7:2.

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} on the noun (L); no setting on the pronouns
alternatives: the setting on the pronouns, as in English
decisions.reason: French puts the gender setting on the noun the Greek has (the human being), not on the pronouns: "lui" and "le" are the same for "l’être humain" and "l’homme". Balanced and Readable say "quelqu’un" and "les gens", already inclusive. Used the same way in 7:18-23.

decisions.choice: "souiller" (L); "rendre impur" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to make common, ritually unclean (meaning decision). Literal keeps one strong verb, "souiller", for it throughout 7:15-23; Balanced and Readable say plainly "rendre impur", the opposite of "pur" in 7:19.

decisions.choice: mtu, yake (L); mtu (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: Swahili "mtu" is any person and "-ake" (his, her) has no gender, so the English span (them, him) has nothing to change in Swahili.

source.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου, ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν παραβολήν.

records.literal_gloss: And when he entered into a house from the crowd, were asking him the disciples of him the parable.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into a house away from the crowd, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [about] the parable.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had left the crowd and gone indoors, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about this parable.
en.R: Jesus left the crowd and went into a house. Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} what this word picture meant.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời đoàn dân vào trong một nhà, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [về] dụ ngôn ấy.
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã rời đoàn dân và vào nhà, các môn đồ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về dụ ngôn ấy.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu rời đoàn dân và đi vào một ngôi nhà. Rồi các môn đồ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lời ví von ấy có nghĩa là gì.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 무리를 떠나 집으로 들어가셨을 때, 그분의 제자들이 그분께 그 비유에 [대하여] 묻고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 무리를 떠나 집 안으로 들어가시자, 제자들이 그 비유에 대해 여쭈었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 사람들을 떠나 어떤 집으로 들어가셨다. 그러자 제자들이 그 비유, 곧 빗대어 하신 말씀이 무슨 뜻인지 여쭈었다.

es.L: Y cuando entró en una casa, lejos de la multitud, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban por la parábola.
es.B: Cuando dejó a la multitud y entró en una casa, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron por esa parábola.
es.R: Jesús dejó a la gente y entró en una casa. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron qué quería decir esa comparación.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut entré dans une maison, loin de la foule, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogeaient sur la parabole.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut quitté la foule et fut rentré dans la maison, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogèrent sur cette parabole.
fr.R: Jésus a quitté la foule et il est entré dans une maison. Alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé ce que voulait dire cette parole imagée.

sw.L: Na alipoingia nyumbani mbali na umati, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakimwuliza [kuhusu] ule mfano.
sw.B: Alipokwisha kuuacha umati na kuingia nyumbani, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza maana ya mfano huo.
sw.R: Yesu aliuacha umati, akaingia ndani ya nyumba. Kisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwuliza mfano huo una maana gani.

decisions.choice: parable: a puzzling saying that needs to be explained
decisions.reason: The parable is the short saying of 7:15. The word can mean a riddle or dark saying as well as a story.

decisions.choice: into a house: away from the crowd, as in 4:10
decisions.reason: Mark does not name the house. As in 4:10-20, Jesus explains his sayings to the disciples in private.

decisions.choice: word picture
decisions.reason: Readable keeps its usual wording for a parable.

decisions.choice: "dụ ngôn" (L, B); "lời ví von" (R) for "parable"
decisions.reason: "Dụ ngôn" is the standard modern word for a parable; "ví dụ", the 1926 word, now means "example". Readable uses a plain phrase for a saying that speaks in pictures.

decisions.choice: "여쭈었다" for the disciples asking Jesus
decisions.reason: The narrative uses the humble verb of asking for questions put to Jesus, matching the honorific "께"; Literal keeps the plainer "묻고 있었다" for the imperfect.

decisions.choice: comparación (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable uses a plain word for a saying that needs explaining (meaning decision m1); Literal and Balanced keep "parábola".

decisions.choice: "cette parole imagée" (R); "la parabole" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short puzzling saying (7:15), not a story (meaning decision); "parole imagée" says that plainly for new readers. "Comparaison" would not fit a saying with no comparison in it.

decisions.choice: mfano (parable) at Readable too
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:23, "mfano" is plain enough for Readable, where the English Readable says "word picture".

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Thus also you without understanding are?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Are you also so without understanding?
en.B: He said to them, "Are even you so slow to understand?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Do even you not understand this?

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Các con cũng thiếu hiểu biết như vậy sao?
vi.B: Ngài nói với họ: "Ngay cả các con mà cũng chậm hiểu như thế sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ngay cả các con cũng không hiểu điều này sao?

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희도 이렇게 깨닫지 못하느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희조차 이렇게 깨닫지 못하느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희도 이것을 깨닫지 못하느냐?

es.L: Y les dice: «¿Así que también {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} sin entendimiento?
es.B: Les dijo: «¿Hasta {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} tan lentos para entender?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «¿Ni siquiera {{plural_you:ustedes entienden|vosotros entendéis}} esto?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Vous aussi, vous êtes ainsi sans intelligence ?
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Même vous, vous êtes si lents à comprendre ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Même vous, vous ne comprenez pas cela ?

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Je, hata ninyi mko hivyo bila ufahamu?
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Je, hata ninyi ni wazito hivyo wa kuelewa?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Je, hata ninyi hamwelewi jambo hili?

decisions.choice: without understanding: unable to grasp the meaning
decisions.reason: The word answers 7:14, where Jesus called everyone to understand. The disciples are no quicker than the crowd (6:52; 8:17).

decisions.choice: a question that rebukes
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the words as a question. Jesus is surprised that his own followers need an explanation.

decisions.choice: "các con" for the disciples
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to his disciples, as in the Vietnamese John; the scene has moved from the crowd ("các người") into the house.

source.text: οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλ’ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν, καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται;

records.literal_gloss: Not you understand that everything from outside entering into the man not is able him to defile, \v 19 because not it enters of him into the heart but into the belly, and into the latrine goes out?

en.L: Do you not perceive that everything entering into the person from outside cannot defile {{gender:them|him}}, \v 19 because it does not enter into {{gender:their|his}} heart but into the belly, and goes out into the latrine?"
en.B: Do you not see that nothing that goes into a person from outside can make that person unclean? \v 19 It does not go into the heart but into the stomach, and from there it goes out into the latrine."
en.R: Do you not see? Nothing that goes into people from the outside can make them unclean. \v 19 It does not go into their hearts. It goes into their stomachs, and then it goes out of their bodies into the toilet."

vi.L: Các con không nhận biết rằng mọi thứ từ bên ngoài đi vào trong con người không thể làm người ấy ô uế sao, \v 19 vì nó không đi vào lòng người ấy nhưng vào bụng, rồi đi ra nơi hố xí?"
vi.B: Các con không thấy rằng không có gì từ bên ngoài đi vào một người mà có thể làm người ấy ô uế sao? \v 19 Vì nó không đi vào lòng mà vào bụng, rồi từ đó ra nơi hố xí."
vi.R: Các con không thấy sao? Không có gì từ bên ngoài đi vào trong người ta mà có thể làm cho họ ô uế. \v 19 Nó không đi vào lòng họ. Nó đi vào bụng, rồi ra khỏi cơ thể, xuống nhà vệ sinh."

ko.L: 밖에서 사람 안으로 들어가는 모든 것이 그를 부정하게 할 수 없다는 것을 알지 못하느냐? \v 19 그것이 그의 마음으로 들어가지 않고 배로 들어갔다가 뒷간으로 나가기 때문이다."
ko.B: 밖에서 사람 안으로 들어가는 것은 무엇이든 그 사람을 부정하게 할 수 없다는 것을 모르겠느냐? \v 19 그것은 마음으로 들어가지 않고 배로 들어갔다가, 변소로 나간다."
ko.R: 모르겠느냐? 밖에서 사람의 몸속으로 들어가는 것은 사람을 더럽게 만들 수 없다. \v 19 그것은 사람의 마음으로 들어가지 않는다. 배 속으로 들어갔다가 몸 밖으로 나가 화장실로 빠져나간다."

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:comprenden|comprendéis}} que todo lo que entra en la persona desde fuera no puede contaminarla, \v 19 porque no entra en su corazón, sino en el vientre, y sale a la letrina?».
es.B: ¿No {{plural_you:ven|veis}} que nada de lo que entra en una persona desde fuera puede hacerla impura? \v 19 No entra en el corazón, sino en el estómago, y de ahí sale a la letrina».
es.R: ¿No lo {{plural_you:ven|veis}}? Nada de lo que entra en la gente desde afuera puede hacerla impura. \v 19 No entra en su corazón. Entra en su estómago, y después sale del cuerpo y va a parar a la letrina».

fr.L: Ne saisissez-vous pas que tout ce qui, du dehors, entre dans {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} ne peut pas le souiller, \v 19 parce que cela n’entre pas dans son cœur, mais dans le ventre, et s’en va dans les latrines ? »
fr.B: Ne voyez-vous pas que rien de ce qui entre du dehors en quelqu’un ne peut le rendre impur ? \v 19 Cela ne va pas dans le cœur, mais dans le ventre, et ensuite part aux latrines. »
fr.R: Vous ne comprenez pas ? Rien de ce qui entre dans les gens depuis l’extérieur ne peut les rendre impurs. \v 19 Cela ne va pas dans leur cœur. Cela va dans leur ventre, et ensuite cela sort de leur corps et va aux toilettes. »

sw.L: Je, hamtambui kwamba kila kitu kinachoingia ndani ya mtu kutoka nje hakiwezi kumtia unajisi, \v 19 kwa sababu hakiingii moyoni mwake bali tumboni, na kinatoka kwenda chooni?"
sw.B: Je, hamwoni kwamba hakuna kitu kinachoingia ndani ya mtu kutoka nje kinachoweza kumfanya najisi? \v 19 Hakiingii moyoni mwake bali tumboni, na kutoka hapo kinatoka nje chooni."
sw.R: Je, hamwoni? Hakuna kitu kinachoingia ndani ya mtu kutoka nje kinachoweza kumfanya najisi. \v 19 Chakula hakiingii moyoni mwake. Kinaingia tumboni, kisha kinatoka mwilini na kwenda chooni."

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, the center of thought and will
decisions.reason: Food goes into the stomach, not into the heart where a person's choices are made (7:21).

decisions.choice: latrine: the place where waste goes
decisions.reason: The word means a privy or toilet. Jesus speaks plainly: food passes through the body and out of it.

decisions.choice: do you not perceive: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: Jesus states what they ought to have seen for themselves.

decisions.choice: toilet
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "뒷간" (L); "변소" (B); "화장실" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is plain but not crude; the older words suit the ancient setting at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the everyday word, as the English Readable says "toilet".

decisions.choice: chooni (into the latrine) at every level
